imperial.name: Cucumber, Outdoor

actions.text:
Sow indoors

Apr–May in warm pots.

Sow

Jun, or late May under cloches.

Plant out

Jun in settled warmth after frost.

methods.text:
Sow in pots 

Sow one seed on edge in each pot at about 70°F. Keep the compost just moist. Harden off gradually.

Plant out 

Water the pot first. Set the rootball intact and level with the soil, then water in. Let stems trail or put trellis in place at planting.

Sow outside 

Sow where the plants will grow once the soil is warm. Cover with a cloche or jar while the seedlings establish.

varieties.text:
STANDARD RIDGE
Marketmore 76

A well-established ridge cucumber for outdoor growing in a warm, sheltered position. Produces dark-green slicing fruits.

STANDARD RIDGE
Bush Champion

A compact outdoor cucumber suited to smaller gardens and large containers. A useful alternative to vigorous trailing selections.

JAPANESE
Burpless Tasty Green

A long-fruited outdoor cucumber for a sheltered summer bed. Provide support where practical and pick fruits regularly.

APPLE
Crystal Lemon

An unusual cucumber with round, pale-yellow fruits. Pick young for the best texture; a novelty alongside a standard slicing variety.

Cucumber, Outdoor.
DIFFICULTY
Medium
3/5
HARVEST SEASONS
Summer / Autumn

Ridge cucumbers need a warm, sheltered bed. Choose an outdoor variety for slicing or gherkins for pickling. Train stems up a trellis if space is short.

Quick facts
Sow indoors

Apr–May in warm pots.

Harvest

Jul – Sep

Germination

6–9 days

Sowing depth

1/2–3/4 in.

Row spacing

4 ft between rows when vines trail over the ground

Yield per plant

10 cucumbers

Plant spacing

2 ft between plants along each row; one plant per prepared site

Ready in

About 12–14 weeks from sowing

Sow

Jun, or late May under cloches.

Plant out

Jun in settled warmth after frost.

Recommended varieties
STANDARD RIDGE
Marketmore 76

A well-established ridge cucumber for outdoor growing in a warm, sheltered position. Produces dark-green slicing fruits.

STANDARD RIDGE
Bush Champion

A compact outdoor cucumber suited to smaller gardens and large containers. A useful alternative to vigorous trailing selections.

JAPANESE
Burpless Tasty Green

A long-fruited outdoor cucumber for a sheltered summer bed. Provide support where practical and pick fruits regularly.

APPLE
Crystal Lemon

An unusual cucumber with round, pale-yellow fruits. Pick young for the best texture; a novelty alongside a standard slicing variety.

Key risks
Mildew

Powdery mildew often appears on older leaves later in the season.

Slugs and snails

Slugs and snails may chew seedlings and low fruit.

Lack of warmth

If sowing or planting conditions are cold, plants grow slowly and become easy prey for slugs, woodlice and damping-off diseases.

Cucumber mosaic virus

Cucumber mosaic virus can cause mottled, puckered leaves, stunting and distorted fruit.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
50
FRUITING CROPS

Wait for real summer warmth.

Outdoor cucumbers are frost-tender and struggle in cold, wet ground.

Keep picking young fruit.

Regular cutting encourages the plant to keep producing.

Soil & preparation
Sunny, sheltered, fertile, moist but drained soil. Enrich pockets with rotted compost.
Allow room to trail or provide a trellis. Keep roots moist and fruit clear of damp soil.
Sowing & planting
Raise in warmth
Plant roots intact
Sow in pots 

Sow one seed on edge in each pot at about 70°F. Keep the compost just moist. Harden off gradually.

Plant out 

Water the pot first. Set the rootball intact and level with the soil, then water in. Let stems trail or put trellis in place at planting.

Sow outside 

Sow where the plants will grow once the soil is warm. Cover with a cloche or jar while the seedlings establish.

Looking after the crop
Weed, water regularly and mulch. Begin organic liquid feeding when fruits swell, especially in containers or light soil.
Open covers before plants overheat. Keep male flowers on ridge types that need pollination and let insects in. Check the packet for all-female varieties.
Train stems up supports or rest trailing fruit on tiles. Pinching after six or seven leaves encourages sideshoots.
Harvesting & storage
Cut regularly before skins toughen and seeds enlarge. Growth slows as autumn cools; harvest remaining usable fruit before frost.
Pick gherkins small, often around 2 in. long for pickling. Discard any unusually bitter cucumber.
Pests & diseases
Problem	What to look for	What to do
Mildew	Powdery growth on older leaves.	Water roots steadily; remove badly affected foliage.
Slugs and snails	Young plants or low fruit are chewed.	Check at night; hand-pick slugs and keep fruit off wet soil.
Lack of warmth	Weak growth in cold, wet conditions.	Wait for warm soil and settled weather.
Cucumber mosaic virus	Mottled, puckered leaves; weak growth.	Remove plants and weeds. Wash hands and tools.
Frost	Leaves blacken and plants collapse.	Plant after frost risk; finish harvesting before autumn frost.
Bitterness	Fruit tastes unusually bitter.	Discard bitter fruit; do not try to make it safe by cooking.
Root rot	Wilting; dark, decaying roots.	Remove collapsed plants; improve drainage and avoid cold wet roots.
Grey mould (Botrytis)	Grey mould on damaged fruit or stems.	Remove infected parts. Air the crop and keep fruit dry.
Final tips

Keep ground-grown fruit off wet soil on clean tiles/boards.

Water roots; handle fragile stems gently when picking/training.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
See also: Vegetable Troubles 117–121 · Growing Techniques 149–150
51
FRUITING CROPS
